parts_missing: unclear whether symptoms are all required; encoding demands all five findings plus one of headache/nausea/vomiting
elements.problem: Acute glaucoma likely is in scope (diagnosis, priority). Rule is a strict AND of pain, red eye, blurred vision, haloes and fixed dilated pupil plus (headache or nausea or vomiting); the page reads as a descriptive list, so requiring every symptom risks missing real cases. Concept 'Acute angle closure' is a UK-extension term under 'Acute disease of eye', acceptable but not named glaucoma. Dosing (acetazolamide) is management, out of scope.
evidence: Diagnose probable acute glaucoma in a patient with eye/vision symptoms :: (and (clinical_finding Pain in eye) (clinical_finding Red eye) (clinical_finding Blurring of visual image) (clinical_finding Sees haloes around lights) (clinical_finding Fixed dilatation of pupil) (or Headache Nausea Finding of vomiting))

Allergic conjunctivitis likely is a probable diagnosis with itch AND (discharge or watery) AND (both eyes, eczema, hayfever or asthma). 'Both eyes' captured via 'Right and left'. 'Hayfever' encoded as 'Allergic rhinitis caused by pollen'. Missing: the 'one eye, no eczema/hayfever/asthma: localised cause likely' branch (no diagnosis concept).
evidence: Diagnose probable allergic conjunctivitis :: (and (or Discharge from eye Watery eye) (clinical_finding Itching of eye) (or (... Right and left) Eczema Allergic rhinitis caused by pollen Asthma))

elements.problem: Contains the stye rule and the discharge decision; stye encoded as lump in eyelid AND eyelid pain (Hordeolum, probable). The 'No itch -> clear or pus?' branching is represented through negation of itch in viral/bacterial rules. The eyelid-problem referral criteria (eyelashes touching cornea, eyelids bent in/out) are not encoded; and the 'eyelid pain' finding is not in the non-urgent task check_for.
evidence: Diagnose probable stye :: (and (clinical_finding Lump in eyelid) (clinical_finding Pain (finding_site Eyelid structure)))

elements.problem: Viral conjunctivitis: no itch, clear watery (serous) discharge, and fever or sore throat or enlarged nodes. Reasonable 'or'. Fever is written as active_condition while the other symptoms use clinical_finding, and Fever is not in the non-urgent check_for.
evidence: Diagnose probable viral conjunctivitis :: (and (no Itching of eye) (clinical_finding Serous conjunctival discharge) (or (active_condition Fever) Sore throat Localized enlarged lymph nodes))

rule_level_problems.problem: Chemical burn and foreign-body concepts are not eye-specific/site-bound; no severe pre-eclampsia diagnosis despite 'treat as severe pre-eclampsia'; no non-urgent routes for superficial foreign body.
Only one priority level (Urgent) used; page justifies this (single red box).

summary: The red box is well covered: nearly all urgent criteria are encoded correctly with valid SNOMED concepts. Most consequential gaps: no severe pre-eclampsia diagnosis, STI 'symptoms' encoded as STI disease, an overly strict all-symptoms glaucoma AND, non-site-specific chemical burn, and the superficial foreign body and eyelid-referral branches are not encoded.
